sections.title: A resolution of the Erdős similarity problem in the large
sections.abstract: For every unbounded set A in the real line and every positive epsilon below one, the author constructs a closed, uniformly large set avoiding every nontrivial affine copy of A, with its unit-interval density tending to one at both ends.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.2 claims that for every unbounded A⊂R, epsilon in (0,1), and R0>0, there is a closed symmetric (1-epsilon)-large set S containing [-R0,R0], with |S∩[x,x+1]|→1 as |x|→∞, such that every nonzero dilation and translate of A has infinitely many points outside S.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A is any unbounded subset of R; largeness means measure at least 1-epsilon in every unit interval. This is the 'in the large' variant of the Erdős similarity problem.
sections.unique_caveat: The original Erdős similarity conjecture for all infinite sets remains open; the paper also shows that the density-convergence rate cannot in general be prescribed independently of A.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The v2 revision adds a deterministic construction; the paper is cross-listed between classical analysis and number theory. Independent mathematical context was found at Wolfram MathWorld and MathAudit; this is not a correctness certificate.

sections.title: A Poisson boundary solution to Connes' bicentralizer conjecture and Kadison's problem on MASA
sections.abstract: The paper develops Poisson-boundary methods for von Neumann algebras and uses them to claim new proofs of bicentralizer conjectures and a solution to a maximal-abelian-subalgebra problem.
sections.claimed_result: For countably decomposable von Neumann algebras M⊂P with a normal faithful conditional expectation, the author claims M⊂c(P) has the weak Dixmier property, yielding a new proof of Connes' bicentralizer conjecture and the relative bicentralizer conjecture. The paper also claims a solution to Kadison's problem under the additional assumptions below.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The weak-Dixmier result assumes countable decomposability and a normal faithful conditional expectation. The MASA result further assumes separable preduals and M'∩P=Z(M); it produces a MASA of M that is also maximal abelian in P.
sections.unique_caveat: These are substantial claims in a 44-page new preprint; their proof and relationship to recent independent work require expert assessment.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract claims results on two major open problems and builds a bridge from Poisson-boundary theory to operator-algebra inclusions; the cross-list adds dynamical systems. Placement reflects potential significance rather than measured uptake.

sections.title: Proof of the polygonal Saint-Venant inequality conjectured by Pólya--Szegö
sections.abstract: For each n≥3, the authors claim that the regular n-gon uniquely maximizes torsional rigidity among all polygons of prescribed area with at most n sides, including non-convex polygons.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1 states that for every n≥3 and every polygon D with at most n sides, its torsional rigidity is at most that of the equal-area regular n-gon, with equality only for congruent polygons. The authors describe an analytic proof using polygon partitions and mixed torsional-rigidity comparisons.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Bounded polygonal domains of prescribed area; the competitor may be non-convex and may have fewer than n sides.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is restricted to polygons and torsional rigidity; it is not a general shape-optimization theorem for arbitrary domains or other functionals.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper claims a full resolution of a conjecture dating to Pólya and Szegö, extending beyond convex polygons; it gives a precise theorem for geometric analysis. No independent attention signal was found in the searches checked.

sections.title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
sections.abstract: The authors disprove the proposed formula for the Davenport constant of C_n^r by giving a strictly larger lower bound for C_6^r when r≥23.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 claims D(C_6^r)≥5r+floor(r/23)+1 for every positive integer r, implying D(C_6^r)>5r+1 for r≥23 and contradicting the conjectured value 5r+1.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite abelian homocyclic groups C_6^r; D(G) is the least sequence length forcing a nonempty zero-sum subsequence.
sections.unique_caveat: The bound is a lower bound for the n=6 family, not an exact determination of D(C_6^r) or a disproof for every n.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors identify the conjecture as a long-standing zero-sum problem from 1969; the result is cross-listed between combinatorics and number theory and gives an explicit family of counterexamples.

sections.title: A disproof of the El-Zahar--Erdős conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors construct graphs of arbitrarily large chromatic number and arbitrarily large girth in which every anticomplete pair has one side of chromatic number at most six, contradicting the proposed large-chromatic-separation property.
sections.claimed_result: For all integers d≥1 and g≥4, the authors prove existence of a graph G with χ(G)≥d and girth at least g such that every anticomplete pair A,B has min(χ(G[A]),χ(G[B]))≤6.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite simple graphs; anticomplete means disjoint vertex sets with no edge between them. Taking g=4 yields triangle-free examples.
sections.unique_caveat: The negative answer uses the fixed threshold seven (equivalently, the upper bound six on one side); it does not classify all possible chromatic thresholds or graph classes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper states a counterexample to a named conjecture, persisting in triangle-free graphs and extending to any prescribed girth. The abstract gives a concrete threshold and a probabilistic construction.

sections.title: Sharpness of the Osgood threshold for anomalous dissipation and non-uniqueness in passive scalar transport
sections.abstract: For every concave non-Osgood modulus of continuity, the authors construct divergence-free transport producing anomalous dissipation and infer non-uniqueness for bounded transport solutions.
sections.claimed_result: For each concave non-Osgood modulus ω, the authors construct a divergence-free velocity u∈L∞([0,1];C^ω(T²)) and smooth initial data for which the advection-diffusion solutions have a positive dissipation anomaly as viscosity tends to zero. They derive non-uniqueness of bounded transport solutions as a corollary.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two-dimensional torus, divergence-free drift, concave non-Osgood spatial modulus; the main construction is time-bounded in C^ω and locally Lipschitz in space before the terminal time.
sections.unique_caveat: The main theorem assumes concavity; the authors note that unrestricted non-Osgood moduli include pathological cases where the corresponding class is effectively log-Lipschitz.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It identifies and closes a sharp regularity-threshold gap, combining anomalous dissipation with transport uniqueness; the paper states explicit function-space conditions. No independent attention evidence was found in the searches checked.

sections.title: A counterexample to Molchan's orthant persistence conjecture
sections.abstract: For the isotropic fractional Brownian field, the author disproves Molchan's proposed persistence exponent in a regime of sufficiently small Hurst parameter and sufficiently large dimension.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves limsup_{d→∞} limsup_{R→∞}[-log p_{d,H}(R)/(d log R)]≤1-(49/48)H+o(H) as H↓0, contradicting the conjectured exponent for sufficiently small fixed H and all sufficiently large dimensions depending on H.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Persistence probability for the isotropic fractional Brownian field on [0,R]^d, with limits taken in the displayed order and H tending to zero.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem does not settle the conjecture for general H or fixed dimension; the author mentions further candidate results, including H=1/2, but does not include their proofs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper states a counterexample to a recognized persistence conjecture and supplies an explicit asymptotic improvement in a high-dimensional, small-Hurst regime. It includes a Gaussian interpolation inequality in an appendix.

sections.title: A Geometric Calderón Problem for Differential Forms
sections.abstract: The authors prove boundary determination and partial-data uniqueness for a geometric Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential forms, with rigidity results under analyticity or harmonic-curvature assumptions.
sections.claimed_result: For Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on p-forms, the authors recover the full boundary jet modulo conformal gauge when n=2p+2 and prove global partial-data uniqueness for analytic metrics and for smooth metrics with harmonic curvature; a Weyl nondegeneracy condition upgrades conformal equivalence to isometry.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact oriented Riemannian manifolds with boundary; partial measurements on a nonempty open boundary subset. Global uniqueness uses interior and measured-boundary analyticity, or alternatively smooth metrics with harmonic curvature; conformal ambiguity remains at n=2p+2.
sections.unique_caveat: The global conclusions depend on the stated regularity/curvature hypotheses, and critical-dimension data determine the metric only up to conformal gauge unless the additional Weyl condition holds.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper connects inverse boundary problems, differential geometry, and elliptic/transport unique continuation, with boundary-jet and global uniqueness theorems. No external discussion was found in the searches checked.

sections.title: Infinite cascades for the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the square torus
sections.abstract: For every 1<s<2, the author constructs a square-torus solution whose H^s norm grows without bound at arbitrarily slow rates as time tends to positive infinity.
sections.claimed_result: For each 1<s<2, the author constructs a solution of the defocusing cubic NLS on the square two-torus with initial data in H^s whose H^s norm tends to infinity as t→+∞, with growth that can be arbitrarily slow; the squared norm tracks selected axial frequencies up to bounded error.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Defocusing cubic NLS on the square two-torus; Sobolev exponent 1<s<2 and initial data in H^s.
sections.unique_caveat: The statement is for this equation, torus, and exponent range; it constructs particular solutions and does not imply generic Sobolev growth.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result exhibits unbounded Sobolev growth for a defocusing nonlinear dispersive equation and extends results described in an earlier version; this is a concrete dynamical construction, not a numerical observation.

sections.title: Two almost sure upper bounds for sums of random multiplicative functions
sections.abstract: The author proves almost-sure upper bounds for partial sums of squarefree and extended Rademacher random multiplicative functions, with a matching-order lower occurrence for one weighted sum.
sections.claimed_result: For every epsilon>0, almost surely |Σ_{n≤x} f(n)/√n|≪(log log x)^{1/4+epsilon} and |Σ_{n≤x}g(n)|≪√x(log log x)^{1/4+epsilon}; for f, values at arbitrarily large x also attain at least (log log x)^{1/4+o(1)}.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: f is a squarefree random multiplicative function and g an extended Rademacher random multiplicative function; the bounds are almost sure as x grows.
sections.unique_caveat: The lower bound is stated only for the weighted f-sum; the paper does not claim matching lower bounds for both upper estimates.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The author describes the work as substantially streamlining and improving a previous version; the number-theory/probability cross-list and almost-sure bounds provide signals of mathematical reach and revision lineage.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
text: Conjectures under pressure by proof and counterexample: Yip, Zhou, Bogosel et al., Gao et al., and Liu–Meng report results in distinct fields; this is not one shared method.
Sharp thresholds and extremal regimes: Liss–Luan–Tan, Novikov, and Atherfold identify specific boundary regimes in PDE or probability/number theory.
Geometry inferred or optimized from restricted data: Jin–Wang treat partial boundary measurements while Bogosel et al. optimize polygonal torsional rigidity; their methods differ.
Energy and frequency transfer in nonlinear evolution: Chen's NLS construction is an isolated signal in this selected batch, not evidence of a wider shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
text: Author-stated: Yip says the original Erdős similarity conjecture for arbitrary infinite sets remains open; synthesis direction: characterize admissible density-convergence rates and test other infinite configurations. Refs: paper-01.

Author-stated: Novikov lists candidate results on existence of persistence exponents and the case H=1/2, with candidate proofs omitted; synthesis direction: prove these limits and quantify the dimension threshold. Refs: paper-07.

Author-stated: Jin–Wang's critical-dimension data have conformal gauge, and a Weyl nondegeneracy condition can upgrade to isometry; synthesis direction: determine necessity and test what additional measurements break the gauge. Refs: paper-08.
Author-stated limitation: Gao et al. give a lower bound, not the exact Davenport constant; synthesis direction: combine sharper lower and upper bounds for C_6^r. Refs: paper-04.
Author-stated scope: Liss–Luan–Tan assume concave non-Osgood moduli; synthesis direction: characterize weakest hypotheses ensuring anomaly and bounded-solution non-uniqueness. Refs: paper-06.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The clearest signal in this batch is a cluster of sharply formulated claims: several long-standing conjectures are reported settled or refuted, alongside new sharp-regime constructions in PDE and probability. Attention and citation data are sparse, so treat the order as a reading shortlist, not a measured popularity table or independent validation.
